# MC-002-INTA-FE-R1 — OpenCode independent source/evidence re-review (packet-only)

**Task:** MC-002-INTA-FE-R1-SOURCE-REVIEW · **Reviewer:** OpenCode (actual independent QA, this session; no subagent). **Models:** reviewer model not independently attested; owner model Gemini 3.8 Flash High (owner-reported per `10-harness-meta.txt`, no attestation). **Scope:** packet-only — no tools, no edits, no runtime, no hash recomputation. Supplied Codex integrity material (5 raw hashes, 5 export hashes, 25 source entries byte-equal raw↔archive, archive 23401 B, template `3e5a642` / backend `52b60a4` clean) is cited as **supplied intake only**. Owner-run results (66 tests / 7 files, 7/7 guard checks, zero upstream measured at synthetic listener) are cited per retained log; **Codex did not replay**; they never set matrix rows. Ledger unchanged: **51 NOT_RUN (36/14/1)**; MC-002 and C01-PRODUCT OPEN.

**VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUIRED** — R01/R05/R06 and most of R04/R08/R09 are genuinely fixed and are preserved; residual source defects keep pre-upstream blockers open (F01, F02, F03, F04) plus guard/teardown correctness before the next evidence-producing run (F06, F07).

## R01..R10 disposition

| Finding | Disposition | Concrete basis (supplied source/evidence) |
|---|---|---|
| R01 | **CLOSED_SOURCE_ONLY** | `src/schemas.ts nativeUserSchema` decodes `created_at`/`updated_at`; `tests/schemas.test.ts` validates native shape and rejects camel-only with explicit field errors. Timestamp format rule moved to driver assertion (correct layer). |
| R02 | **PARTIALLY_RESOLVED** | Driver assets now exist (36-ID list, runId validation/generation, collision refusal, checkpoint rules for T1/T2, truncation blocking). But `src/driver.ts` is a 304-line exported class: no main/entry, no fetch, never calls `executeCase`, no phase dispatch, no one-attempt ledger, checkpoint only in memory, `persistEnvelope` overwritable, `pauseForUpstreamCoordination` never invoked by route/executor and only mutates a string. `"driver": "node src/driver.ts"` executes nothing. Return §2's "full harness-local driver asset" overstates; F01. |
| R03 | **PARTIALLY_RESOLVED** | Persistence across restart/hot-reload/runId switching works via `counters.json` + per-runId `generators` Map; tests prove it. Residual: load errors fall back to `0` and write failures are silently ignored → duplicate-ID risk; read-modify-write non-atomic; stale overlapping instance can overwrite a higher counter with a lower in-memory seq; driver preflight checks `counters-<runId>.json` while the real file is `counters.json`, and `HarnessDriver` constructor ignores its custom `stateDir` in preflight. F02. |
| R04 | **CLOSED_SOURCE_ONLY** | Vocabulary `value/apiError/abort`, `classification` (`unavailable` for 503/status 0/TIMEOUT), single-sourced wire body, measured versions present. Residual identity-authenticity risk is new: F03. |
| R05 | **CLOSED_SOURCE_ONLY** | Byte-accurate truncation via `findSafeUtf8TruncationIndex`/`truncateUtf8` verified in source; CJK/emoji/object/details tests present; details capped; `truncated` cross-surface flag correct. |
| R06 | **CLOSED_SOURCE_ONLY** | 15 required / 8 forbidden refId table enforced pre-dispatch in `harnessCaseInputSchema` (400, zero upstream); T5/T8 readbacks unconditional; 23-case test table present. |
| R07 | **PARTIALLY_RESOLVED** | Startup refusal implemented in `next.config.ts` via `validateHarnessStartup`, generic refusal text, audited secret keys enumerated. Residuals: config guard skips when `NODE_ENV=test`/`VITEST` — a bypass the frozen §2 does not contain (and unit tests import guards directly, so it is unnecessary); empty-string env counts as "set" per frozen literal but is accepted; return lists `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME` as refused while the guard omits it. F04/F05. |
| R08 | **PARTIALLY_RESOLVED** | Isolated dimensions with valid runIds `inta20261025a`, computed per-check verdicts, measured zero upstream at 18086, owned-PID stop script exist. Residuals: Check 7 treats exit code `null` as pass and leaks child 3 on timeout; unexpected paths lack finally cleanup; `stop-harness.sh` accepts `0`/negative/non-numeric PIDs (group-signal risk) and claims-but-lacks port verification; Check 1 headers printed but unasserted. F06/F07/F08. |
| R09 | **CLOSED_SOURCE_ONLY** | T5/T8/T6-W/T7-W/W9 descriptions corrected; 503-only enforced; real installed versions (16.4.2/19.3.1/5.9.3/9.39.5 per intake); `PREPARED (Harness only)` label; all 36 IDs incl. INT-ENV-05/06/07 present. Wording/scope riders → F08/F09 (doc-only). |
| R10 | **CLOSED_SOURCE_ONLY** | Wire `AbortSignal.timeout(10000)`; `import.meta.dirname`; typed `refusedKeys`; direct template import documented; truncation type-change documented. |

## Findings (stable IDs MC-002-INTA-FE-R1-F01…)

**F01 — P0, pre-Go/PG blocker — executable driver/phase coordinator still missing (R02 residual).**
`path: src/driver.ts:HarnessDriver` (also `package.json:scripts.driver`). No entry point: cannot sequence the 36 IDs, cannot enforce one-attempt-per-substep, cannot gate upstream, cannot restore checkpoints. Per-case assertion rules exist only for T1/T2: missing T9 (version 2 + updated name probably vs checkpoint), T10 readback preservation, T11a/b/T12/W11 unavailable + native literals (`/problems/unavailable`, integer retryAfter 1), wire rules (ETag `"1"`/`"2"`, `Location` == B id, `x-request-id` echo == envelope requestId, `application/problem+json` for W3/T6-W/T7-W/W11), per-case RFC-3339/UUID re-assertion on T5/T8/T9/T10/PERS readbacks. T1's `UUID_LOWERCASE_REGEX` accepts any version (contract binds lowercase UUIDv7) and never checks expected fixture email/name against the normalized response. `PersistEnvelope` overwrites `<caseId>.json`; checkpoint is memory-only — a dev reload or mid-run restart loses state.
**Minimal fix:** smallest harness-local runner script (e.g. `scripts/run-phase.ts` + npm target) invoking one frozen §6 phase per owner run; explicit upstream enable gate (e.g. `MC_INTA_ENV_READY=1` validated in `guards.ts`, refusal = bounded 503/409 with zero upstream) plus manual owner checkpoint confirm between phases — this is the "pause", no contract edit; write-once envelope persistence (refuse overwrite unless byte-equal) and durable write-once checkpoint under `.run-state/checkpoints/<runId>.json` restored on construction; add the assertion-rule table per case; never implement Go/PG lifecycle in FE — phase scripts print external-owner handoff prompts only. **Regression:** runner refuses without gate; duplicate-case POST refused by ledger; reload/restore test; T1 normalized-email rule test.

**F02 — P1, must fix before any correlation run — counter fail-closed + atomicity + preflight alignment (R03 residual).**
`path: src/request-id.ts:loadPersistedSeq/persistSeq` + `route.ts:generators`. Concrete: (a) load/parse failure → seq 0 → IDs collide with previously persisted IDs for the same runId; (b) write failure silently ignored → later boot replays a lower counter; (c) non-atomic `readFile+writeFile` can yield a torn `counters.json`, feeding (a); (d) a stale overlapping module instance advances in-memory seq and unconditionally overwrites `data[runId]` downward. Minimal, no distributed locking, frozen format kept (no boot nonce needed if fail-closed + atomic): throw on unreadable/unparseable counters (fail closed, zero upstream), temp-file+rename write (same-directory, overwrite), throw on write failure; align `assertNoRunIdCollision` to check the real `.run-state/counters.json` (plus envelope dir) and have `HarnessDriver` pass its `stateDir` into the preflight. **Regression:** corrupt/missing counters → refusal not 0; simulated overlapping stale generator — no downward overwrite; runId-switch tests still pass.

**F03 — P1, must fix before any envelope-producing run — identity metadata can silently fabricate provenance.**
`path: src/executor.ts:getInstalledNextVersion/getHarnessRevision`. Exact: env overrides `MC_INTA_NEXT_VERSION` / `MC_INTA_HARNESS_REVISION` are returned without any validation against the installed package or actual source; the Next fallback is literal `'16.4.2'` and the harness-revision fallback is literal `e25bbc6…` — the **base** commit, not R1 head `6e2f65b5…`. Envelope identity fields would then read as measurements that are neither. Return §2 (R04) claims "dynamically resolves git HEAD" — true only when `.git` exists; archive-exported runs silently record the base commit. **Minimal fix:** drop env overrides (or mark values `identity-source:override` explicitly — removal is smaller); replace literal fallbacks with an `unmeasured:<reason>` sentinel and record identity-check-missing (or refuse substeps) in R2; qualify the §R04 wording. **Regression:** unit — env set does not alter recorded value; no-git cwd → sentinel + refusal, no historical literal.

**F04 — P1, must fix before INT-ENV-05 acceptance evidence — contract-literal deviations in startup refusal.**
`path: next.config.ts:guard-skip; src/guards.ts:validateHarnessStartup/validateHarnessEnvironment`. (a) The conditional `NODE_ENV !== 'test' && !process.env.VITEST` is an invented bypass absent from frozen §2 and serves no test necessity (unit tests import the guard functions directly; `next.config` is not loaded by them) — call the guard unconditionally. (b) Refusal keys skip empty strings; frozen literal "any product auth/bypass env **set**" — refuse on presence (`env[key] !== undefined`) so `API_MODE=""` refuses. **Regression:** add unit+live cases: `NODE_ENV=test` + `API_MODE=demo` → refusal; `API_MODE=''` → refusal; live production-attempt check (Check 7b) still owed at runtime QA.

**F05 — P2, documentation-only — refused-vs-audited key-list alignment (R07 rider).**
`return §R07 vs src/guards.ts:PRODUCT_AUTH_ENV_KEYS`. Do **not** add `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_NAME` (public UI-name key, not session/secret; adding it would be new unneeded policy). Correct the return to distinguish "refused" (`API_MODE`, `API_TOKEN`, `API_BASE_URL`, `AUTH_ALLOW_ANONYMOUS`, audited secret keys) from "audited, documented-only". `API_TIMEOUT_MS` is currently refused — keep, but document the deliberate harness-local rationale once. No code change.

**F06 — P1, must fix before the next guard-evidence capture — Check 7 machinery and owned-cleanup hygiene.**
`path: scripts/live-guards.ts:Check7/main`. Exact: `startupExitCode` starts `null`; `pass = startupExitCode !== 0` — a hung start whose 5 s timeout resolves yields `null !== 0` → **PASS with unknown exit** (false refusal evidence); on that timeout path child 3 is never killed; `main()` catch exits 1 without closing the upstream observer or stopping spawned children; no `finally` cleanup. Also no live check exercises the NODE_ENV=production refuser (unit-only today). **Minimal fix:** require a numeric non-zero exit; `devProcess3.kill('SIGTERM')` on timeout; wrap phases in try/finally closing observer and stopping owned PIDs; add production-attempt live check in R2. Regression: timeout-while-booting case now FAIL, not PASS; clean-exit path unchanged (7/7 should remain reproducible).

**F07 — P1, must fix before teardown evidence — `stop-harness.sh` PID trust.**
`path: scripts/stop-harness.sh`. Exact: `TARGET_PID` accepts `0`, negative, non-numeric; on an empty/`0`/negative PID file, `kill -0`/`kill -TERM` can target the **caller's process group** (group signal), never claim an unrelated process was actually killed — currently nothing cross-checks ownership; the script (and return §R08) claims port-18085 verification but contains none. **Minimal fix:** strict `^[1-9][0-9]*$` validation before any kill signal; record provenance at guard-start (PID + `ps -o lstart=` + command path) in a sibling file and refuse mismatch at stop; add the claimed port check or drop the wording; keep SIGTERM→bounded 5 s→SIGKILL. Regression: `0`/`-1`/`abc`/stale-mismatched PID → refuse with manual guidance, zero signals sent.

**F08 — P2, evidence/doc — assertion and scope wording riders.**
(a) `live-guards.ts:Check1` prints `cache-control`/`allow` but `pass` does not assert them — either assert both (1-line) or stop describing Check 1 as header-verified. (b) "Port 18085 never opened": a closed-at-check snapshot plus config-load error supports *refusal before ready*; qualify the wording (the return may keep the config-error-position evidence, not "never listened" as a proven absolute). (c) INT-ENV-07 marked PREPARED "tested under webpack dev": cross-root compile is genuinely evidenced (the route loads the unchanged template client in the live guards run), but no-fetch-caching/reuse and all remaining INT-ENV-07 assertions are runtime only — scope-qualify; rows stay NOT_RUN.

**F09 — P2, documentation-only — provenance qualification of retained artifacts (R09 riders).**
Retained logs contain narrative wrapper frames over (apparently) real command output; hashes match as supplied but cannot attest raw-capture fidelity alone — the R2 return should label segments "owner wrapper" vs raw stdout without alleging anything. `live-guards.ts` executes `fetch` and prints `curl …` equivalents — label printed lines as equivalents, not executed argv (exact spawn argv for the dev server is present and correct). `13-template-isolation.log` evidences only template-clean + typecheck/lint; INT-ISO-02 full artifact-exclusion inspection remains runtime QA. INT-PRIV-01 scan scope (owner logs) remains prep-only; Go/Next app-log scan deferred to runtime. Model identity remains owner-reported.

## Blocker grouping

- **Must fix before any Go/PG case execution:** F01, F02, F03, F04.
- **Must fix before the next evidence-producing guard/teardown run (can proceed in parallel):** F06, F07; fold F08(a) into the same re-capture.
- **Documentation-only (companion return/R2 review docs):** F05, F08(b)(c), F09.
- **Non-blocking, no new findings.**

## Material architecture deviation?

**No.** All residuals are ordinary implementation/evidence defects within the frozen INTA-1 boundaries: harness-local runner, counter persistence semantics, identity measurement, and refusal mechanics tied to the frozen literal. No INT-A0/B/C switch, no contract edit, no product/template/backend change, no Claude conformance escalation required. The F01 gate, F04 removal of the invented bypass, and F05's refusal-not-adding are aligned with, not contrary to, frozen §2/§3.

## Preserved R1 improvements (fix scope must not regress)

Native snake_case schema + camel rejection tests; byte-accurate 16 KiB truncation incl. CJK/emoji/details; 23-case refId table with mandatory T5/T8 readbacks; computed guard verdicts with valid runIds and measured zero upstream via a synthetic observer; owned-PID stop script concept; fixed-URL generic refusal; per-runId generators Map; wire timeout 10 s; corrected 36-ID inventory and installed versions.

## Skipped and remaining risk

Skipped: hash recomputation (supplied hashes cited, not verified), any execution/test/build, Go/PG runtime, guards re-capture, and review of files outside the supplied packet. Remaining risk: (1) F01 means the 36-case sequence still cannot be executed as-driven — sequencing/assertion gaps (T9/T10/503/wire-header rules, checkpoint durability, one-attempt ledger) may only surface when the runner is first exercised at runtime; (2) identity fabrication (F03) and counter fallback (F02) would corrupt evidence silently if the run starts before fixes; (3) guard and stop-script residuals (F06/F07) affect acceptance evidence quality and owned-process safety; (4) all 51 rows remain NOT_RUN, feasibility unproven until INT-ENV-07 and coordinated Sections B–E execute.
